script: A single teaspoon of neutron star would weigh billions of tons on Earth. Neutron stars form when a giant star's core collapses in a supernova. They pack more mass than the Sun into a ball only about 20 kilometers wide. Some spin more than 700 times every second. Drop something from just one meter above the surface, and it would hit at about 2000 kilometers per second. Follow WonderBytes for more facts that sound fake but are true.

description:
Neutron stars are the collapsed cores of giant stars: more mass than the Sun packed into a ball about 20 km wide. A teaspoon of their material would weigh billions of tons, the fastest known one spins 716 times a second, and something dropped from one meter would hit the surface at about 2,000 km/s.
